The high winds had allowed the fire to travel “extremely quick and cover an area of almost six miles in less than 24 hours”, he added.
Joe Lombardo, the Nevada governor, declared a state of emergency and called the blaze an “active and rapidly evolving situation”.
Shane Akerson, a battalion chief with the Truckee Meadows Fire Protection District, said the fire was “human-caused”.
“However, that is still undergoing active investigation and we don’t have further details provided at this time,” he said.
A dangerous heatwave is sweeping seven US states with temperatures soaring as high as 118F (47.7C) in Phoenix, Arizona.
The National Weather Service’s Weather Prediction Centre issued an extreme heat warning for an area spanning from Louisiana to California.
summary: Wildfires in Reno have grown to over 15,000 acres with zero percent containment, driven by high winds that allowed the fire to move rapidly. Nevada Governor Joe Lombardo declared a state of emergency in response to the active blaze, which officials stated was human-caused and remains under investigation. Meanwhile, a dangerous heatwave with temperatures reaching up to 118F is affecting seven US states under an extreme heat warning.
key_points: The Reno wildfire has burned over 15,000 acres with zero percent containment.
Nevada Governor Joe Lombardo declared a state of emergency.
Officials stated the fire was human-caused, though the investigation is ongoing.
An extreme heat warning covers an area from Louisiana to California with temperatures reaching up to 118F.

title: US removes Syria from list of state sponsors of terrorism
author: Tom Bateman; Helen Livingstone
content:
![Two men in dark suits and red ties smile and shake hands in front of windows and American flags](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/999/cpsprodpb/0972/live/c3169dc0-a016-11f1-b109-879e35c24276.jpg)
US President Donald Trump welcomed his Syrian counterpart Ahmed al-Sharaa to the White House last year
- Published
The US has removed Syria from its list of state sponsors of terrorism after 47 years, lifting what it said was the "final major barriers" for private sector investment in the country and its reintegration into the global economy.
US Secretary Of State Marco Rubio said the move was in recognition of the Syrian government's positive actions to fully distance itself from acts of international terrorism.
The Trump administration has embraced Syria's new president, Ahmed al-Sharaa, a former militant who once had an American bounty on his head as the leader of an al-Qaeda off-shoot.
His Islamist group, Hayat Tahrir al-Sham (HTS), was also removed from the US list of global terrorist organisations.
HTS, formerly known as al-Nusra Front, was al-Qaeda's affiliate in Syria until Sharaa severed ties with the jihadist network in 2016.
In late 2024, HTS led the rebel offensive that overthrew former president Bashar al-Assad and it dominates Sharaa's transitional administration.
The US hopes to bring Syria into its orbit rather than that of Russia or China. But the risks remain significant, with Syria still far from secure and lacking representative government. It is also at the centre of growing tensions between its neighbours Israel and Turkey.
Rubio said Monday's move, which had been initially flagged in July, would give the Syrian "a path to prosperity".
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said: "Today's action will help foster additional investment in Syria to promote political and economic stability."
Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad Hassan al-Shaibani greeted the news as a "historic step", according to state-run news agency SANA.
"We will continue working to remove the effects of isolation and create an environment based on transparency, mutual interests and respect," he said.
Last year, the US also revoked the designation of HTS as a Foreign Terrorist Organisation and removed Sharaa from its list of Specially Designated Global Terrorists.
Syria's removal from the US list of state sponsors of terrorism - where it had been since 1979 - leaves just three remaining: Cuba, North Korea and Iran.
The listing carries financial sanctions, restrictions on US foreign aid and defence exports and sales and can also penalise people and other countries that trade with the sanctioned state.
summary: The United States has removed Syria from its list of state sponsors of terrorism after 47 years, lifting major barriers to private sector investment and global economic reintegration. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated the decision recognizes Syria's efforts to distance itself from international terrorism under its new president, Ahmed al-Sharaa. The Trump administration also removed al-Sharaa's Islamist group, Hayat Tahrir al-Sham (HTS), from the US list of global terrorist organizations.
key_points: Syria was removed from the US state sponsors of terrorism list after being on it since 1979.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio cited Syria's positive actions to distance itself from international terrorism.
Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa and his group HTS were also removed from US terror lists.
The policy change aims to lift barriers to private investment and help integrate Syria into the global economy.

title: Diner's disgust at receipt telling chef to ‘burn and spit on her eggs'
author: Barney Davis
content:
![Italian restaurant in Riccione under fire after an incident involving 17 year old waiter and owner joking about the incident with another customer](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_309360492-5734-e1787593596281.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
An Italian restaurant wrote, ‘This is p***ing me off. Burn [her] eggs and spit in them’ after a tourist complained they were runny.
Clara had been visiting the Victor Lab, in Romagna, Italy for breakfast with her family last week.
But when the Brazilian mum’s scrambled eggs, juice, and coffee arrived she asked her teenage server if the eggs could be ‘a little more cooked’.
He reportedly scoffed, ‘we don’t make raw eggs here’ before taking them back to the kitchen, La Voce di Cesenatico reported.
‘In the end, they arrived very soft, but I didn’t ask for them to be recooked,’ the diner, who refused to reveal her surname after getting death threats, said.
![Italian restaurant in Riccione under fire after an incident involving 17 year old waiter and owner joking about the incident with another customer](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_309361965-9f8c.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=543) 
Sign up for all of the latest stories
‘I let it go because I didn’t want to argue,’ Clara said.
But when it was time to pay she noticed something peculiar with her receipt.
In Italian, it read: ‘This is pissing me off. Burn the eggs and spit in them.’
She claimed her family became ‘scared’ over the possibility of their food getting saliva seasoning.
After telling the 17-year-old waiter she understood the message, he reportedly went ‘as white as a sheet’ and tried to throw the receipt away. But Clara told him she would call the police if he did.
She went viral after posting the receipt under a scathing one-star Google review of the restaurant.
A manager then apologised under the comment saying: ‘The behavior you reported was absolutely inappropriate and in no way reflects the values, customer service, and professional standards we strive to ensure every day.’
After the altercation blew up on social media the Victor Lab seized their chance to capitalise, trying to joke on a video on their TikTok account.
![Italian restaurant in Riccione under fire after an incident involving 17 year old waiter and owner joking about the incident with another customer](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_309360405-1efd.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
The owner is filmed pretending to be a demanding diner ordering a dish with added ‘spit’ in an attempt to make light of the situation.
- 
	![ABC News coverage of the Second Inauguration of Donald Trump airs Monday, January 20, 2025 on ABC. (ABC/Jose Alvarado, Jr.) Barron Trump](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_309359472-58f9.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646&h=363&crop=1)
- Drunk Brit, 30, admits pulling down underwear and 'squatting' on packed plane
- Five youngsters who died after crashing into police car pictured
- Twelve arrested after deadly A66 crash that killed seven
They even added a poll asking customers whether the 17-year-old server should be sacked.
‘Sometimes it almost makes you laugh when you watch it, but this isn’t a laughing matter.
‘It’s serious,’ said Clara, adding she had received racist threats on social media.
summary: An Italian restaurant in Romagna faced backlash after a tourist named Clara discovered an insulting note on her receipt instructing the chef to burn and spit on her eggs. Clara had asked her teenage waiter to cook her scrambled eggs a bit more, prompting the inappropriate kitchen instruction to be printed on the bill. After the incident went viral from a one-star Google review, the restaurant issued an apology and later posted a TikTok video attempting to make light of the situation.
key_points: A tourist visiting Victor Lab in Italy requested her scrambled eggs to be cooked a little more.
When receiving her bill, she found a receipt stating in Italian to burn the eggs and spit in them.
The 17-year-old waiter went pale and tried to throw away the receipt when confronted.
The restaurant management initially apologized online but later posted a mocking TikTok video about the incident.
The diner reported receiving racist death threats and social media backlash following the viral post.

title: US threatens severe sanctions against countries with economic ties to Iran
author: Julian Borger
content:
The US has threatened to impose severe sanctions against any country or entity maintaining economic ties with Iran, hoping to achieve with economic measures what military means have so far failed to do.
It is unclear, however, how far the Trump administration is prepared to go in confronting China, Iran’s biggest trading partner, which has signalled its resistance to US economic pressure to cut off links with an ally.
Iran, meanwhile, vowed retaliation against any country that took part in the US-led isolation campaign.
Launching what he called Operation Economic Outcast, the US treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, called it an unprecedented campaign and compared it with the D-day Normandy landings, a turning point in the second world war.
“Today, in that same spirit, we are launching an economic onslaught against Iran’s financial connections around the globe,” Bessent said on Monday. “Our objective is to sever every economic lifeline that sustains this tyrannical regime until Tehran stands alone.”
Asked whether sanctions would be applied to China, which bought an estimated 80% of Iran’s shipped oil last year, he replied: “We want to make clear here today that no one is above the reach of US sanctions. That if they facilitate transactions and are part of the ecosystem that turns Iranian oil into money, into repression, they will be targeted.”
Bessent said the US had identified those that continued to deal with Iran and each violator would be given a deadline to cut ties or face US sanctions. He said the deadlines imposed would depend on individual circumstances.
“Any entity that facilitates money laundering on behalf of Iran will be removed from the US dollar system,” he said. “The clock just started ticking.”
Bessent said Donald Trump was “making phone calls to world leaders with specific requests to cease their interactions with the regime”, but he did not specify whether the US president would talk to his Chinese counterpart, Xi Jinping.
China’s embassy in Washington told reporters: “Regarding the Iran issue, sanctions and pressure do not help resolve the problem. China calls on the relevant parties to take responsible actions and resolve the issue through political and diplomatic means.”
Tehran said it would retaliate against the sanctions using a range of measures. Maj Gen Ali Abdollahi, the armed forces’ chief of staff, said the retaliation could take the form of land, sea or air operations or cyber-attacks.
The announcement of secondary sanctions against Iran comes nearly six months after the the US and Israel launched an attack on Iran that killed its supreme leader Ali Khamenei. Early expectations that the regime in Tehran would collapse or agree to Washington’s demands to give up uranium enrichment and other key elements of its nuclear programme were dashed.
Hardliners appeared to strengthen their grip on government in Tehran and responded by declaring the closure of the strait of Hormuz, attacking ships that ignored its declaration. Trump imposed a counter-blockage on Iranian oil exports through the strait, leading to an impasse that has had profound effects on the global economy.
Sina Toossi, a senior non-resident fellow at the Center for International Policy, said: “After nearly six months without a military or diplomatic victory, Washington appears to be trying to accomplish through intensified economic strangulation what military force has so far failed to achieve. But Tehran is answering that zero-sum approach with one of its own.”
The US defense secretary, Pete Hegseth, however, said further military action was not off the table. “By no means are we foreclosing using kinetic strikes anywhere in the strait of Hormuz or around Iran,” Hegseth told reporters on Monday.
In apparent anticipation of the US measures, the United Arab Emirates, a close US and Israeli ally, announced it was suspending trade ties with Iran. Turkey, another trading partner with Iran, which has been critical of the US-led campaign against the Islamic Republic, has yet to respond to the US threat of sanctions.
Andrew Miller, a senior fellow at the Center for American Progress, said: “The announcement of new economic sanctions on Iran and those countries trading with it signals what is plain to all: this war has brought the United States no closer to eliminating Iran’s nuclear programme or crippling the Iranian regime. But while sanctions can be effective, it is highly unlikely they will produce a quick settlement favourable to the United States.”
summary: The US has launched "Operation Economic Outcast," threatening severe secondary sanctions against any country or entity maintaining economic ties with Iran. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that violators will face deadlines to sever ties or risk being removed from the US dollar system. Meanwhile, Iran has vowed military and cyber retaliation, and China—Iran's largest trading partner—has signaled resistance to the US pressure.
key_points: The US announced a new campaign of severe economic sanctions targeting any country or entity trading with Iran.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned that entities facilitating transactions for Iran will be removed from the US dollar system.
China, Iran's biggest trading partner and buyer of most of its shipped oil, has signaled its resistance to US pressure.
Iran's armed forces chief of staff vowed that Tehran would retaliate against the sanctions through land, sea, air, or cyber operations.
The United Arab Emirates announced it was suspending trade ties with Iran in apparent anticipation of the US measures.

title: US-Canada trade war heats up as Trump threatens to hike auto tariffs
author: Nadine Yousif
content:
![US President Donald Trump delivers remarks outside the White House. He is speaking at a podium with the US presidential seal at the front. He is wearing a dark navy blue suit and a yellow tie. Behind him are several US flags.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/999/cpsprodpb/59dc/live/1a42fea0-9ff8-11f1-be19-71b839ccdc73.jpg)
Donald Trump accused Canada on Monday of "ripping America off", threatening to hike US tariffs on Canadian autos in the new year
- Published
President Donald Trump has threatened to hike US tariffs on automobiles originating in Canada, as the trade war between the two neighbours continues to heat up.
Trump said on Monday that he will increase tariffs on Canadian cars and trucks, as well as auto parts, from 25% to 50% as of 1 January.
It comes after US-Canada trade talks collapsed late last week, with each side accusing the other of making unreasonable last-minute demands.
Prime Minister Mark Carney called Trump's latest levy threat unsurprising and accused the president of wanting to destroy Canada's auto industry. He added that Canada is ready to resume talks if the US comes with the "right attitude".
Watch: Canada will negotiate if US has the "right attitude", says Mark Carney
The war of words followed several US and Canadian officials saying that talks are suspended with no set date to resume.
Trump's threat was the latest escalation after Canada walked away from trade negotiations late Friday night, moments before a US-imposed deadline that would add a 50% levy on nearly $20bn (C$28bn; Â£14bn) of Canadian imports.
The collapse in talks marked a significant change in tone from earlier in the week, when both sides appeared optimistic that a new US-Canada trade deal could be reached.
Canadian officials have said that the US introduced last-minute demands that were "unacceptable", including a clause limiting which countries Canada could sign trade deals with.
US officials, meanwhile, said that it was Canada that introduced last-minute changes. "They wanted more," US trade representative Jamieson Greer said in an interview with CNBC on Monday.
The breakdown led to growing tensions as both sides publicly dug in their heels.
On Monday, Trump's tariff threats to Canada's auto industry followed Carney declaring the country would counter his levies with reciprocal tariffs on US goods "dollar for dollar".
Carney said he was focused on supporting Canadian businesses impacted by new 50% US tariffs after the Friday deadline expired, as well as building infrastructure to diversify Canada's trade, which historically has relied heavily on the US.
Carney announced funding of C$11bn ($7.95bn; Â£5.83bn) to build six icebreakers at a Quebec shipyard for the Canadian Coast Guard that will replace its medium and heavy ageing fleet.
The icebreakers will be used to open winter shipping routes through Canada's northern and Atlantic waters.
'Trump underestimates us': Doug Ford takes aim at US over tariffs
Meanwhile, Ontario's outspoken premier, Doug Ford, whose province is home to Canada's auto manufacturing industry, responded to Trump's tariffs and threats by telling the US president to "kiss my ass".
Ford also suggested that Canada should charge the US extra for its oil and gas, as well as electricity and critical minerals, adding that he will be speaking to Carney on ways to "fight back".
His comments appeared to catch the attention of Trump, who in a Truth Social post accused Ford of "bluster" and wrote: "Someone should get these clowns to 'fall in line' or, the consequences for Canada will be far WORSE!".
Canada accounts for 60% of total US crude oil imports and close to 100% of US natural gas exports, according to Canadian government data.
Businesses on both sides have warned that they stand to be impacted by the new wave of US tariffs on Canada, as well as the "dollar-for-dollar" retaliatory tariffs that Canada plans to impose on 8 September.
The trade war also put into question the future of an existing North American trade pact, known as the UMSCA, that was signed by Trump in his first term with Canada and Mexico.
During a mandatory review this summer, both Canada and Mexico said they want the USMCA extended for another 16 years. The US, however, said it will not renew in its current form.
The pact underpins $1.6tn in North American trade.
Experts with Oxford Economics warned on Monday that a dismantling of USMCA could have dire economic consequences for Canada.
"While unlikely, escalating trade tensions means the risk of the USMCA unravelling has increased, which would plunge Canada into recession and leave it on a permanently lower growth path," warned Head of Canada Economic Tony Stillo and Senior Economist Michael Davenport.
Watch: "Absolutely ridiculous": Canadians react to new tariff tensions with the US
summary: The trade war between the US and Canada escalated after trade talks collapsed following mutual accusations of unreasonable last-minute demands. President Donald Trump threatened to increase tariffs on Canadian autos from 25% to 50% starting January 1. In response, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced plans for reciprocal tariffs and infrastructure investments, while Ontario Premier Doug Ford suggested retaliating by charging the US more for energy and critical minerals.
key_points: US-Canada trade talks collapsed after both sides blamed each other for introducing unacceptable last-minute demands.
President Donald Trump threatened to hike US tariffs on Canadian cars, trucks, and auto parts to 50% on January 1.
Prime Minister Mark Carney stated that Canada will counter US levies with dollar-for-dollar reciprocal tariffs on US goods.
Ontario Premier Doug Ford suggested that Canada should charge the US extra for oil, gas, electricity, and critical minerals.
Escalating trade tensions have raised concerns about the potential unravelling of the USMCA trade pact.

title: Mother who lost arm in shark attack says she remembers every second
author: Lily Shanagher
content:
![Leah Stewart, with her partner Fernando, describes her shark attack ordeal to 60 Minutes Australia](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/world-news/2026/08/24/TELEMMGLPICT000499432319_17875929214470_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqKMHqiEQqDqDVNuTOclNc-nGTJFJS74MYhNY6w3GNbO8.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Leah Stewart, with her partner Fernando, describes her shark attack ordeal to 60 Minutes Australia](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/world-news/2026/08/24/TELEMMGLPICT000499432319_17875929214470_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqKMHqiEQqDqDVNuTOclNc-nGTJFJS74MYhNY6w3GNbO8.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
An Australian mother who lost her arm after being bitten by a shark said she could remember every second of the attack.
Leah Stewart, a schoolteacher, was mauled by a suspected 12ft great white shark in June while taking a morning swim between the flags at Coogee Beach in Sydney.
The mother of one was critically injured, suffering life-threatening bites to her arms and legs.
She was placed into a medically induced coma for nearly a fortnight, had multiple surgeries and her arm amputated.
The 35-year-old told 60 Minutes Australia she remembered the entire ordeal and that she encouraged herself to try to survive after thinking of her daughter, August.
Ms Stewart said: “Its face was horrific – I will never forget its face. It was a monster. It was holding on to my leg.”
She said she told herself “I’ve got to fight it and do everything I can to be here” after thinking of her baby daughter.
“All I was thinking of was August and I thought, ‘She’s not going to have a mum’,” Ms Stewart said. “I couldn’t handle that. I did not want her not to have a mum.”
In the interview, which airs next Sunday, an emergency call made at the time is played in which operators are told: “We’ve got a shark attack on Coogee Beach… There’s a lot of blood in the water.”
In the aftermath of the attack, a fundraiser to help support Ms Stewart’s recovery and pay for a prosthetic arm raised around $558,000 (£300,000).
Created by her brother Josh Stewart, the fundraiser said Ms Stewart had suffered “multiple bites across her arms and legs, lacerations and fractures throughout her body, and extreme blood loss”.
![Emergency personnel attend to Ms Stewart  at Coogee Beach](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/world-news/2026/08/24/TELEMMGLPICT000490177465_17875931831430_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqpVlberWd9EgFPZtcLiMQf0Rf_Wk3V23H2268P_XkPxc.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
In an update shared on Sunday, Ms Stewart said she was turning off donations as she had received enough to “recover, to stay in our home, and to give us options for further medical treatment down the road”.
She added that she felt as though she had been given “a second chance at life, and I’m not going to waste it.
“As I get better, I know I’ll make something of this second chance and aim to give back even more in generosity, care and love. I will forever be grateful for everything, and everyone, I’ve been given.”
Australia has seen several deadly shark attacks this year, with four people attacked in two days in January, including a 12-year-old boy who was fatally wounded.
Experts say there has been a modest increase in the number of shark attacks in the past two decades.
The rise has been attributed to a number of factors, including coastal population growth, climate change and more people taking part in water sports.
summary: Australian mother and schoolteacher Leah Stewart recalled every second of a harrowing shark attack at Sydney's Coogee Beach in June, which resulted in the amputation of her arm and critical injuries. Thinking of her young daughter, August, gave her the will to fight and survive the mauling by a suspected 12-foot great white shark. Following the attack, a fundraiser raised approximately $558,000 to support her recovery and medical treatments before donations were recently closed.
key_points: Leah Stewart, a 35-year-old mother and schoolteacher, was critically injured in a suspected 12-foot great white shark attack at Coogee Beach in June.
She suffered severe bites to her arms and legs, spent nearly two weeks in a medically induced coma, and had her arm amputated.
Ms Stewart stated she remembers every second of the ordeal and fought to survive because she did not want her baby daughter, August, to grow up without a mother.
A fundraising campaign raised around $558,000 for her recovery and prosthetic arm before donations were recently turned off as sufficient funds were reached.

title: Ukraine’s allies convene in Kyiv as Zelenskyy seeks air defence boost
author: Al Jazeera Staff
content:
![Britain's Prime Minister Andy Burnham looks at Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky deliver a speech during a commemorative ceremony marking Ukraine's 35th Independence Day outside St. Sophia cathedral in Kyiv, Ukraine, August 24, 2026. HENRY NICHOLLS/Pool via REUTERS](https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/2026-08-24T104301Z_892133695_RC2Y4NASTE5M_RTRMADP_3_UKRAINE-CRISIS-COALITION-BURNHAM-1787569192.jpg?resize=770%2C513&quality=80)
Ukraine will host a meeting with its key European allies to discuss air defence and press for greater pressure on Moscow as Russia continues to escalate missile attacks.
The “Coalition of the Willing” meeting in Kyiv will be jointly chaired by the leaders of France and Germany, who will join remotely, and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who arrived in the Ukrainian capital early on Monday.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items
- list 1 of 3Photos: Ukraine celebrates National Flag Day
- list 2 of 3Russia, Ukraine trade attacks as Putin warns of ‘far more destructive’ hits
- list 3 of 3Putin warns Ukraine has opened ‘Pandora’s box’, rejects peace proposals
European Council President Antonio Costa is also attending in person.
![UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham lays flowers at the tomb of the unknown Ukrainian soldier during a ceremony at Ukraine's national military memorial cemetery as the country marks the 35th anniversary of its independence, in Hatne southwest of Kyiv on August 24, 2026 \[Henry Nicholls/Pool via Reuters\]](https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/2026-08-24T085935Z_1192808379_RC2W4NAHH1BG_RTRMADP_3_UKRAINE-CRISIS-COALITION-BURNHAM-1787566404.jpg?w=770&resize=770%2C513&quality=80)
Kyiv is expected to seek additional interceptor missiles from allies after weeks of Russian missile and drone attacks that have driven record numbers of the capital city’s residents to metro stations and basements to seek shelter.
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has made frequent public appeals for more air defence supplies from allies.
The meeting takes place on Ukraine’s Independence Day and comes a day after the country marked National Flag Day, when a group of leaders from Nordic and Baltic countries met Zelenskyy in Kyiv and pledged to boost their support for Ukraine.
Norway said it would provide another 85 billion kroner ($9.1bn) in 2027, matching the support it gave Ukraine this year.
Escalating air attacks
Russia and Ukraine have escalated air attacks with drones and missiles in recent weeks, striking targets far beyond the front line.
Ukraine has increasingly targeted Russian logistics sites, carrying out attacks on locations linked to e-commerce companies Wildberries and Ozon.
Ozon reported fires early on Monday at its warehouses in four cities including Krasnodar and Makhachkala, both in southern Russia, adding that sites in Adygeysk and Nevinnomyssk were evacuated due to threats of drone attack.
Russian authorities said two children were killed and nine other people were wounded, including seven minors, when drone debris hit a private childcare centre in Krasnodar on Monday. Debris also fell on apartment buildings and set warehouses alight in the city, Governor Veniamin Kondratyev said.
In the Stavropol region, which hosts many chemical production facilities, Governor Vladimir Vladimirov said a drone attack on an industrial area had been repelled early on Monday.
In Ukraine, at least two women were killed and five people injured when a Russian drone hit an electric train in the Kharkiv region on Sunday, regional officials said. An attack on the outskirts of Kharkiv city killed three people and injured eight.
Ukraine’s allies have pledged to boost Ukraine’s depleted air defences in the face of Russia’s growing missile attacks.
Before the meeting, Zelenskyy said deliveries of crucial Patriot interceptors had halved since 2023.
“Over the entire of 2023, Ukraine received 675 missiles, and over all of 2025 – 364, even though Russian missile strikes have increased,” he said.
“For 2026, as currently projected, it is 264,” he added, saying Ukraine was seeking a package of at least 300 for the upcoming winter.
summary: Ukraine is hosting key European allies in Kyiv for a "Coalition of the Willing" meeting to discuss air defence enhancements and increased pressure on Moscow amid escalating missile attacks. The meeting coincides with Ukraine's 35th Independence Day and follows recent pledges of financial and military support from Nordic, Baltic, and other European leaders. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is pressing allies for additional interceptor missiles as deliveries have steadily decreased since 2023.
key_points: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and European Council President Antonio Costa are attending the Kyiv meeting in person, while the leaders of France and Germany are joining remotely.
Ukraine is seeking a package of at least 300 Patriot interceptor missiles for the upcoming winter, noting that deliveries have dropped from 675 in 2023 to a projected 264 for 2026.
Norway recently pledged an additional 85 billion kroner ($9.1bn) in support for Ukraine in 2027.

Recent escalations in air attacks have resulted in casualties and infrastructure damage on both sides, including drone strikes on Russian warehouses and childcare facilities, and a Russian drone strike on a Ukrainian electric train.

title: Trump announces new 50% tariff on Canadian cars, trucks and steel
author: Gaya Gupta
content:
Donald Trump announced a new 50% tariff on automobiles and crucial raw materials from Canada, the latest deterioration in trade relations between the two neighbors with historically strong economic ties.
The US president said that the increased tariffs would start on 1 January 2027 on all cars, trucks, automobile parts and steel. He also derided the nation’s tariffs on American farmers, writing on social media that Canada has been “ripping off” the US “for years”.
“On Trade, and in other ways, also, they are among the worst Nations in the World to deal with,” he wrote on Truth Social. “They feel entitled, and yet, WE DON’T NEED CANADA, THEY NEED US! They do 95% of their business with the U.S., with us, the exact opposite!”
In response, Mark Carney told reporters on Monday that Trump’s announcement was largely expected.
“It’s not a surprise for us that the US would take some form of reprisal to our response to their unjustified tariff, which was on top of other unjustified tariffs,” the Canadian prime minister said from Quebec.
“But what message does that send to the workers in Michigan, in Ohio, in Kentucky, in Alabama, who rely on Canadian demand?” Carney continued. “We’re their largest customer for automobiles, more than the European Union, Japan, Korea, many others combined, and the United Kingdom.”
He added that Canada would be ready to move forward with talks “when the Americans go to the negotiating table first with the right attitude toward our industry and a true partnership”.
Trump’s announcement follows the last-minute collapse this weekend of a potential deal to lower tariffs on automobiles and other materials. After Trump imposed another 50% tariff on $20bn worth of Canadian exports, including hockey equipment and electronics, Carney, rejected the latest deal between the two nations on Saturday.
Carney said that the US “asked too much and they offered too little”, and he has vowed to match the American tariffs “dollar for dollar”.
Canada and the US have been longtime partners, trading roughly $909bn, according to the office of the US trade representative. But Trump’s second presidential term and his aggressive trade policies have brought the era of “deep ties” between the two nations to a close, Carney said last year, vowing to fight Trump’s sweeping tariffs.
summary: Donald Trump has announced a new 50% tariff on Canadian cars, trucks, auto parts, and steel, effective January 1, 2027, citing unfair trade practices. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney responded that the move was expected following the collapse of a potential tariff-reduction deal over the weekend. Carney stated that Canada is prepared to match U.S. tariffs and will await a proper negotiating stance from the United States.
key_points: Trump announced a 50% tariff on Canadian automobiles, auto parts, and steel starting January 1, 2027.
The announcement follows the weekend collapse of a potential deal intended to lower existing tariffs.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney stated that Canada expected the reprisal and will match U.S. tariffs dollar for dollar.
Carney emphasized that Canada remains the largest customer for U.S. automotive exports.
Canada stated it will return to talks only when the U.S. approaches the negotiating table with a true partnership attitude.

title: Live: Trump wants to 'destroy' Canada's auto industry, Carney says of latest tariff threat
author: Live Reporting Edited by Lisa Lambert; Kathryn Armstrong; With Jessica Murphy Reporting
content:
![](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/128/cpsprodpb//vivo/live/images/2022/10/25/418c7f58-8c68-4069-97e8-712f1a94232c.jpg.webp) Eloise Alanna
BBC News
Taking shelter from the rain beneath the entrance to Montreal's Bonsecours Market, Kim and Harry Murphy, - a married couple visiting from Delaware - say they were dismayed by the tariff tensions between Canada and the US.
"We hate what's happening in our country," says Kim, who described the dispute as "insane". Harry adds that the couple had found themselves apologising to Canadians during their trip.
Despite the political tensions, both say they had been met with warmth and kindness throughout their visit.
While hopeful that relations between the two countries can eventually recover, Kim says rebuilding trust, particularly in Canada, could take time.
Harry says he believed ties would return to normal in the future, adding that he remained optimistic about the long-standing friendship between the neighbouring nations.
![A man and a woman wearing rain gear smile at the camera, he has his arm around her](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/640/cpsprodpb/vivo/live/images/2026/8/24/f8b8e1cd-02e4-4d02-a55b-d5ca7ac4cbbb.jpg.webp)
summary: American tourists visiting Montreal expressed dismay over ongoing tariff tensions between Canada and the United States. Despite the political friction, the couple reported receiving warmth and kindness from Canadians during their trip. They remain hopeful that relations and trust between the two neighboring nations will eventually recover.
key_points: A married couple from Delaware visiting Montreal shared concerns over US-Canada tariff tensions.
The visitors reported being met with warmth and kindness by Canadians despite the political disputes.
The couple expressed optimism that long-standing ties between the two countries would eventually return to normal.
They noted that rebuilding trust in Canada following the tensions could take some time.

title: Trump administration announces ‘economic D-day’ sanctions on Iran
author: Al Jazeera Staff
content:
![U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent speaks during a press conference to outline further sanctions against Iran, at the Treasury Department in Washington, D.C., U.S., August 24, 2026. REUTERS/Evelyn Hockstein TPX IMAGES OF THE DAY](https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/reuters_6a8c7daf-1787592111.jpg?resize=770%2C513&quality=80)
US Secretary of Treasury Scott Bessent has announced an economic pressure campaign against Iran, vowing to target Tehran’s financial interests across the world.
Bessent said on Monday that the US would target all of Iran’s sources of revenue, including oil, with the aim of preventing other countries and companies from doing business with Tehran.
“Around the globe, our objective is to sever every economic lifeline that sustains this tyrannical regime until Tehran stands alone,” he said.
He said countries around the world must choose between the US and Iran, stressing that the new campaign exposes Tehran’s trade partners to secondary penalties.
Bessent emphasised that “no one is above the reach of US sanctions”.
If countries and entities “facilitate transactions and are part of the ecosystem that turns Iranian oil into money, into repression, they will be targeted”, he said.
The campaign is dubbed “Operation Economic Outcast”. Bessent also called it “economic D-day”, likening it to the Allies’ forces landing on French shores to push back against Nazi Germany during World War II.
The economic pressure campaign comes nearly six months into the war with Iran after the US and Israel launched strikes against the country without direct provocation.
While US and Israeli attacks have killed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and several other top officials, they have failed to dislodge the governing system in Tehran.
Tehran has responded to the US and Israeli strikes with missile and drone attacks across the region. It has also largely shut down and asserted control over the Strait of Hormuz, a major artery for global energy, sending oil and gas prices soaring.
Multiple rounds of fighting and diplomacy have failed to resolve the crisis.
Monday’s sanctions push is the latest effort by the US to pressure Iran to make major concessions, including giving up its nuclear programme and ceasing attacks on vessels in Hormuz.
In April, the US announced a blockade on Iranian ports, but Iran has remained defiant despite the naval siege.
“The blockade has clearly hurt Iran, especially its oil exports, but it hasn’t produced the political outcome Washington wants. Iran hasn’t capitulated,” Sina Toossi, a fellow at the Center for International Policy, told Al Jazeera.
“Hormuz remains heavily disrupted, and the costs to the US and global economy are mounting. So, ‘economic D-Day’ looks like an effort to intensify the pressure now that the military campaign has failed to deliver a decisive outcome.”
Bessent said US President Donald Trump has been making calls to world leaders “with specific requests to cease their interaction with the regime”.
“Those who stand with the United States will reap the rewards of our partnership. Those who tether themselves to the Iranian regime should expect to share in the isolation,” he said.
The US officials said new sanctions will target “five of Iran’s most vital lifelines”: digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping.
The US Treasury also imposed fresh sanctions on 60 entities, vessels and individuals across the world – including in the United Arab Emirates, Hong Kong, China, Singapore and Switzerland – accusing them of enabling the “Iranian regime’s recklessness”.
summary: The Trump administration has announced a new maximum pressure economic campaign against Iran, dubbed "Operation Economic Outcast" or "economic D-day," aiming to sever Tehran's global financial lifelines. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that the campaign will target all of Iran's revenue sources, including oil, and impose secondary penalties on any international trade partners. This escalation follows six months of ongoing conflict and failed military attempts by the US and Israel to dislodge Tehran's governing system.
key_points: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced the new sanctions campaign, targeting Iran's global financial interests and all revenue sources like oil.
The campaign exposes international entities and countries doing business with Iran to secondary penalties and demands they choose between the US and Iran.
New sanctions target five vital sectors: digital assets, technology, gold, aviation, and shipping, along with 60 entities, vessels, and individuals worldwide.
The economic push comes after a six-month military campaign by the US and Israel failed to dislodge Iran's governing system despite killing top officials.

title: Iran claims there is a $10 million bounty on Barron Trump
author: Brendan Rascius
content:
Iranian state media has claimed there is a $10 million bounty on Barron Trump, President Donald Trump’s 20-year-old son, according to a new report nearly six months into the U.S. war with Iran.
Footage broadcast on Channel 3, which is linked to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, was titled “Where and how should we kill Barron Trump?” Euronews reported Monday.
It reportedly displayed the location of his university, as well as Secret Service positions and escort vehicles, while claiming his whereabouts were “fully monitored.”
The clip also claimed that an unnamed young woman had evaded Secret Service protection, met privately with Barron Trump and relayed information about him to the video’s creators. It also claimed he uses Xbox to communicate privately.
Euronews reported that it did not independently verify the claims. The Independent has contacted the White House for comment.
![Iranian state media has claimed there is a $10 million bounty on Barron Trump, the president's 20-year-old son, according to a new report](https://static.independent.co.uk/2026/08/24/14/36/Screenshot-2026-08-24-at-10-52-39-AM.png)
Barron Trump, the president’s youngest son and his only child with First Lady Melania Trump, is a college student. Compared to the president’s other sons, he has kept a relatively low public profile. He has attended some official events, including the president’s UFC cage match at the White House in June and the State of the Union address at the Capitol in February.
This is not the first time he has been targeted by Iran. Last month, an Iran-linked video threatened both Barron Trump and the first lady. The clip, titled “Where to kill Melania” shows a mock up of the first lady’s motorcade and calls on “freedom fighters” to take action against her. It concludes with: “Barron Trump, wait for us!” 
“The Secret Service is aware of the video and investigates anything that can be perceived as a threat toward our protectees,” an agency spokesperson told Newsweek.
![Compared to his older brothers, Barron Trump has kept a relatively low public profile. Pictured: President Donald Trump, first lady Melania Trump and Barron Trump watch during an indoor inauguration parade at Capital One Arena on January 20, 2025 in Washington, DC](<https://static.independent.co.uk/2026/08/24/16/27/GettyImages-2194973757-(1).jpeg>)
The president also has faced repeated threats from Iran over the years, with U.S. officials warning that Tehran and its proxies could seek retaliation for his 2020 order to kill Iranian General Qassem Soleimani. The threats have led to heightened security for Trump and several former members of his administration, though Iran has denied plotting to kill him.
This year, Asif Merchant, a Pakistani business owner, was convicted after authorities accused him of working on behalf of Iran with the intention of carrying out assassinations, with Trump being a target. And in 2024, federal authorities charged Farhad Shakeri, an Iranian national, with taking instructions to develop a plan to kill Trump.
Following the outbreak of the U.S.-Iran war, threats have intensified. At a NATO summit last month, Trump reportedly ditched Air Force One and departed Turkey on a military plane amid concerns about threats from Iran.
The 80-year-old president has said he has “left instructions” if he is killed by Iran “to just literally bomb them at levels that they’ve never seen before.”
![Earlier this summer, a large billboard also cropped up in Tehran depicting Trump being strangled alongside the statement: ‘Revenge is inevitable’](https://static.independent.co.uk/2026/08/24/15/56/GettyImages-2287197505.jpeg)
The newly reported threat against Barron Trump comes as the U.S. war with Iran shows no signs of abating.
Early in the conflict, U.S. forces killed Iran’s longtime supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, along with multiple other senior officials. Trump has since claimed that so many Iranian leaders have been killed that there is “nobody” left to negotiate with.
To date, 18 U.S. service members have been killed in the war and hundreds more have been wounded, the Pentagon has said. Thousands of Iranians have been killed, according to HRANA, a U.S.-based human rights group.
Multiple recent polls indicate a majority of Americans are opposed to the war.
summary: Iranian state media broadcast footage claiming there is a $10 million bounty on Barron Trump, the 20-year-old son of President Donald Trump, amid an ongoing U.S. war with Iran. The video displayed details regarding his university location and Secret Service positions, though Euronews reported it could not independently verify the claims. The Secret Service stated it is aware of the video and investigates any perceived threats toward its protectees.
key_points: Iranian state media broadcast a video titled 'Where and how should we kill Barron Trump?' featuring a claimed $10 million bounty.
The broadcast displayed Barron Trump's university location, Secret Service positions, and escort vehicles.
The Secret Service stated it is aware of the footage and investigates potential threats against protectees.
This follows a previous Iran-linked video from the prior month that threatened both Barron Trump and the first lady.
The threats occur during the ongoing U.S. war with Iran, which has included leadership casualties on both sides.

title: Iran vows to retaliate against countries that cooperate with fresh US sanctions
author: Patrick Wintour
content:
Tehran has vowed to retaliate against any country that cooperates with the US attempt to impose fresh sanctions against Iran in what the Treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, has billed as “the single greatest financial offensive ever marshalled against an adversary”.
In advance of the US announcement, the United Arab Emirates, Iran’s single biggest trading partner in the Middle East, announced it was ending all trade with Iran, a move Tehran believes was coordinated between Washington and the UAE.
The US has said it will impose sanctions on any country or entity trading with Iran – what are known as secondary sanctions.
The test of the US rhetoric is likely to rest on whether countries such as India, China and Russia believe continued trade with Iran would lead to credible US reprisals against their economies. China has for decades been the main importer of Iranian oil.
In May, the US threatened sanctions against Chinese refiners and the banks funding them, but the Chinese commerce department directed Chinese firms to ignore US warnings over Iranian oil imports, saying the threats were illegitimate and deploying for the first time a government statute designed to render US sanctions ineffective in Chinese jurisdictions.
The US had imposed sanctions on Hengli Petrochemical (Dalian) Refinery Co in April but Washington largely backed off as Donald Trump realised he was risking a wider trade and tariff war with China that the US was likely to lose.
This time the Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson, Lin Jian, again said China opposed unilateral sanctions that lacked basis in international law and China believed that military means, sanctions and pressure tactics were not the solution.
However, unlike in May, Iran’s oil shipments to Asia have already all but ended due to the effectiveness of a US naval blockade of Iranian ports, driving the cost of those cargoes to the highest levels in years. Last week, Iran’s central bank governor, Abdolnaser Hemmati, admitted his country’s crude exports had “virtually stopped” due to the US blockade.
The White House believes the Iranian economy is as a result once again on the brink of collapse due to hyperinflation and lack of foreign exchange income caused by the US blockade of oil exports. The rial was trading at 1.992 million per dollar on the unregulated market on Monday, down 4.5% since the US president announced a “crushing economic operation” against Tehran last week.
“Iran is completely collapsing!!!” Trump posted on social media in capital letters on Monday.
![A vessel in the distance as a group of people paddle in the sea in the foreground](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/5ad3be6b4261f831cfc57ed0d27c86ecb88473dd/0_0_6031_4021/master/6031.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
But Iran has been under some kind of US economic maximum pressure campaign for more than 20 years and so far survived.
Iran’s security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, said Tehran would respond with an “earthquake-like” retaliation if Washington proceeded with the proposed measures. He also warned Iran’s Gulf neighbours against joining the US sanctions campaign.
“If the countries surrounding Iran join the Americans in their economic war, not a drop of oil will leave the Persian Gulf and the strait of Hormuz,” Rezaei said, adding that Iran would also target other oil export routes from the Gulf.
Shipping through the strait remained severely disrupted over the weekend, putting further pressure on global energy markets.
Iran’s foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, dismissed the expected sanctions as a sign of US desperation, arguing that the measures would fail to defeat Tehran. He said the US had shifted from military operations to what he described as “the same old plans”.
Reza Nasri, an international lawyer with links to the Iranian foreign ministry, said: “The announcement is not a measure against Iran. It is a claim of jurisdiction over the world, and every sovereign state on Earth is its real addressee. Iran is merely the occasion. The demand that no country allow its own banks, businesses, airports or ship registries to engage in lawful trade with another country is aimed at everyone else. Sovereignty itself is the target.”
Esmail Baghaei, the Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson, said: “Repeating methods that have previously proven to fail will not produce any different results, except that it shows the extent to which America is hostile and spiteful towards each and every Iranian, because it knows very well that the effects of these sanctions will affect ordinary Iranian citizens.”
He added: “Obliging or intimidating other countries to stop or limit their trade relations with another country means violating the most important foundation of international relations and the most fundamental pillar of the United Nations charter, which is respect for the national sovereignty of countries.”
Hassan Ahmadian, a professor of west Asian studies at the University of Tehran, said: “There isn’t a single new sanction. Everything in Iran has been under primary and secondary sanctions since 2018. Since these sanctions failed to achieve the goals the US and Israel wanted, both sides turned to military action. The big fanfare about an ‘economic war’ is really just a public admission of a major step backward. After failing militarily, Washington is clearly stepping back to square one – the economy.”
![A man walks past a billboard which shows Trump underwater reaching for a dollar bill that is hooked on the end of a fishing line](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/c6eb22962838ee258b98b8a56e042464de714209/0_0_4962_3260/master/4962.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
He said Iran had been signalling in recent weeks that US economic warfare was no longer an acceptable option for Tehran and it would prefer going to war rather than standing idly by in the face of the US implementing the blockade. He said this involved “Iranian calculations related to military capabilities, the American domestic situation, and the Iranian domestic situation”.
Last Thursday Bessent claimed in an interview with CNBC that “the US will lead the Islamic Republic of Iran to collapse with the toughest sanctions in history”.
The Treasury secretary claimed “the US government is asking its allies and the rest of the world to stop trading with Iran”. He added that the US “will use all its power against anyone who does not comply with this demand”.
“Either the countries are with us or against us,” Bessent said. “It is time for our allies and the rest of the world to decide, and we will destroy the economy of this regime.” Writing in the Financial Times on Sunday, he said: “Total financial isolation can obviate the need for American force while enlarging the sphere of freedom for our allies. Those who sever Iran’s remaining financial and commercial connectivity will reinvigorate their own. They will deepen their access to global capital, reinforce confidence in their markets and attain the standing they seek in the world economy.”
But China and Russia have so far shown no interest in succumbing to US pressure.
By coincidence, Pakistan’s army chief, Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, flew to Tehran on Monday where he will explore the opportunity to revive talks on the stalled memorandum of understanding signed in June, but not implemented either by Iran or the US largely due to a dispute about whether the memorandum granted Iran interim control over shipping in the strait of Hormuz.
summary: Iran has vowed to retaliate against any country that cooperates with a new wave of stringent US economic sanctions and a naval blockade aimed at collapsing the Iranian economy. The United Arab Emirates has already announced it is ending all trade with Iran, while US officials demand that the rest of the world halt commercial ties or face secondary sanctions. Iranian officials warned that if Gulf neighbors join the US campaign, Iran will block oil exports from the Persian Gulf, further straining global energy markets.
key_points: The US Treasury has marshalled new financial sanctions and secondary measures intended to force the total financial isolation of Iran.
The UAE, Iran's largest regional trading partner, announced it is ending all trade with Tehran.
Iran threatened severe retaliation against any country cooperating with the US sanctions, including blocking oil shipments from the Persian Gulf.
A US naval blockade has effectively halted Iran's crude oil exports, pushing the Iranian economy toward hyperinflation and collapse.

title: Reno wildfire: Tens of thousands told to evacuate as Hawk wildfire approaches Nevada - live updates
author: Live Reporting Edited by Matt Spivey
content:
Satellite imagery shows the impact of the Hawk wildfire in the high desert valley surrounding Reno in Nevada.
Large plumes of smoke can be seen above the city and there is a large patch of scorched land between White Lake and the city.
Officials say around 15,000 acres (23 sq miles) have been burned.
As it stands, the immediate "go now" evacuation zone and wider "get set" area do not extend to the centre of Reno, but do affect large urban areas and part of a highway.
![Satellite image showing smoke and burned land from wildfires west of Reno, Nevada. Cloud covers much of the area around the city, but smoke from fires are visible near the charred ground near White Lake. An inset map locates the scene within Nevada in the western United States.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/640/cpsprodpb/vivo/live/images/2026/8/24/d1031572-6d68-4e20-a8a6-b619544bebbe.png.webp)
summary: The Hawk wildfire has burned approximately 15,000 acres in the high desert valley near Reno, Nevada, producing large plumes of smoke visible from satellite imagery. Tens of thousands of residents have been ordered to evacuate as the fire approaches the city. While the immediate evacuation zones do not extend to downtown Reno, they impact large urban areas and a section of a highway.
key_points: The Hawk wildfire has scorched around 15,000 acres of land between White Lake and Reno, Nevada.
Satellite imagery shows large plumes of smoke and charred land in the region.
Tens of thousands of people are under evacuation orders as the fire approaches.
Evacuation zones currently affect large urban areas and part of a highway, though not downtown Reno.

title: Iran faces 'greatest financial offensive ever', says US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent
author: Mitchell Labiak; Michael Race
content:
![US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's head and shoulders in profile. He has grey hair and glasses. He is wearing a grey suit with a US flag lapel pin, a silver tie, and a white shirt. Behind him in soft focus are US flags and a podium.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1024/cpsprodpb/500a/live/a3b77c00-9fa4-11f1-bff6-57f1422ebb0b.jpg)
- Published
The US treasury secretary has threated Iran with "the single greatest financial offensive ever", claiming the US-Israel war with Iran was "entering its endgame".
Scott Bessent said the US would sever all economic ties with the country in "an economic D-Day" and that any nation partnering with Iran financially would also be isolated.
Bessent's threat to the Iranian regime follows several U-turns and extended deadlines from US President Donald Trump's administration on previous threats.
Iran dismissed Bessent's comments and said it would shut down all oil exports from the region "if the war continues", according to news agency Reuters.
The Iranian regime has also issued a new warning to shipping not to pass through the Strait of Hormuz without its permission, the agency reported.
One fifth of the world's oil and gas usually passes through strait, a waterway south of Iran, but the flow has been effectively blocked by the country since the conflict began at the end of February.
Bessent made the comments in an opinion piece for the Financial Times, external. He did not detail what the economic pressure on Iran would involve, but he is expected to do so in a press conference in the US at 13:00 local time (18:00 BST) on Monday.
"The world should understand that our objective is to sever every economic lifeline that sustains the tyrannical regime until Tehran stands alone," he wrote in the piece.
The US has made several threats to Iran over the course of its war with the country, including Trump saying in April that "a whole civilisation will die tonight" unless Iran agreed a deal to end the war and unblock the Strait of Hormuz.
The US eventually climbed down from that position after mediator Pakistan intervened and called for more diplomacy.
The economic impact of the Iran war is being felt in the US and across the world. Higher oil prices have fuelled concerns over the cost of living, with petrol and diesel prices much higher than they were a year ago.
In the US, gasoline prices have surpassed $4 a gallon and affordability is among the top concerns of American voters ahead of the mid-term elections in November.
Last week, Bessent announced the US government would intervene in the bond markets and buy back more government debt in a bid to boost demand for bonds and lower borrowing rates.
But the impact of the annoucenment was short-lived, with long-term borrowing costs bouncing back up a day later.
The Iranian regime already faces tough economic sanctions from the US.
Former US president Barrack Obama and several US allies had agreed a deal with the country in 2015 which lifted many sanctions in return for Iran agreeing to limit its nuclear programme.
However, Trump pulled out of that deal in 2018, calling it "defective at its core, and reimposed all US sanctions on Iran.
During Joe Biden's term as US president, he made some attempts to reinstate the Obama-era deal, but this did not happen.
In April this year, the Trump administration launched a wave of sanctions on foreign banks and firms doing business with Tehran after it became clear its military operations had not caused Iran's regime to surrender.
summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has threatened Iran with unprecedented financial isolation, stating that the US will sever all economic ties and penalize nations partnering with Tehran. In response, Iran dismissed the comments and threatened to shut down regional oil exports while restricting passage through the Strait of Hormuz. The ongoing conflict and blocked strait have driven up global energy prices, impacting voters and increasing cost-of-living concerns in the US.
key_points: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced plans for a major financial offensive to sever Iran's economic lifelines.
Iran threatened to halt all regional oil exports and warned shipping against using the Strait of Hormuz without permission.
The ongoing war and blocked strait have led to higher global oil prices, with US gasoline prices exceeding $4 a gallon.
The US administration previously implemented various sanctions and threats against Iran after former President Donald Trump withdrew from the 2015 nuclear deal in 2018.

title: Russia's second-biggest online retailer Ozon targeted in Ukrainian strikes
author: James Gregory
content:
![A screengrab from a video on social media showing flames rise from an Ozon facility following a Ukrainian drone strike in Makhachkala, Dagestan, Russia.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1200/cpsprodpb/f16b/live/039a8ff0-9fa4-11f1-bff6-57f1422ebb0b.jpg)
- Published
Warehouses belonging to Russia's second-largest online retailer have been hit by a wave of Ukrainian drone strikes.
Ozon said its logistics facilities in the southern regions of Krasnodar, Dagestan, Stavropol and Adygea were on fire and several people had been injured following overnight strikes.
Ukraine has for weeks struck sites belonging to Wildberries, the country's biggest online retailer, describing the firm as a legitimate target because it supplied components to the military, which Moscow denies.
Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Saturday that Ukraine had opened "Pandora's box" by striking economic targets and that Russia would hit back at Kyiv's "most sensitive economic sectors".
Russia has targeted Ukraine's civilian infrastructure since launching its full-scale invasion in 2022, and recent Russian attacks have hit Ukrainian warehouses and cargo terminals.
Both Russia and Ukraine deny deliberately targeting civilians.
Ozon said "a fire broke out" at a logistics centre in Makhachkala, in the southern region of Dagestan, following a drone attack at around 05:00 local time (02:00 GMT) on Monday.
The company said earlier that a "major fire" was burning at one of its logistics centres in the city of Krasnodar, 700km (435 miles) to the east of the Dagestan site.
Russia's defence ministry said three children had been killed in Krasnodar following a Ukrainian drone attack. Russia's children's rights commissioner Maria Lvova-Belova said they were aged 13, 15 and 16, while six more children had been taken to hospital.
Meanwhile, Ozon workers in Adygeysk, in the Adygea region, and Nevinnomyssk, in the Stavropol region, have been evacuated.
Videos posted on social media of the Ozon attacks have been verified by the BBC. One shows a drone hitting a warehouse in the Orenburg region, while another shows a large plume of smoke and flames rising from its warehouse in Dagestan.
Shares in Ozon fell by as much as 12% on the Moscow Exchange on Monday morning, while shares in its major shareholder, private equity firm AFK Sistema, fell by almost 13%.
When asked on Monday whether the Russian government would provide state support to Ozon, the Kremlin said it was "working with business representatives to develop various options for providing support in this difficult situation".
The overnight strikes comes a day after Ozon's site in the Samara region was hit. The company said a number of its workers had been injured.
Following that strike, Ukraine's defence ministry said on Saturday: "Systematic strikes on dual-use goods storage centres complicate the enemy's logistics and negatively affect the Russian economy as a whole.
"After Ukrainian units hit 15 of the largest logistics hubs of Wildberries, it was Ozon's turn."
Meanwhile, in Ukraine's Odesa region, overnight strikes targeted food storage facilities and energy infrastructure leading to five people being injured, the region's head Oleg Kiper said on Telegram.
Founded in 1998, Ozon is one of Russia's first online retailers. The company is second only to Wildberries in terms of scale and presence, with its pick-up posts and delivery boxes stationed across the country.
Both the Ozon and Wildberries logos are often seen together in Russia at shared pick-up points.
The targeting of these online retailers has had the effect of bringing the war closer to ordinary Russians.
Both companies have been described as "Russia's Amazon" and it is estimated that they are used by 85-90% of Russia's economically active population.
In many remote places lacking accessible shops, Russians depend on them for much of their clothes and household appliances.
But unlike Amazon, which sells goods directly alongside its marketplace business, Wildberries and Ozon act almost entirely as marketplaces, connecting independent sellers with buyers across Russia, storing and delivering their goods and handling payments.
This means many of the losses incurred in the attacks have been borne by those businesses.
The Kremlin has denied that online platforms are used for army supplies.
summary: Warehouses belonging to Russia's second-largest online retailer, Ozon, caught fire and suffered injuries following a wave of overnight Ukrainian drone strikes across southern regions including Krasnodar, Dagestan, Stavropol, and Adygea. Russian officials reported that three children were killed in Krasnodar, while Ozon's shares fell by up to 12% on the Moscow Exchange. The attacks follow similar strikes on Russia's top online retailer, Wildberries, as Ukraine targets major logistics hubs to impact Russian supply lines and the economy.
key_points: Ukrainian drone strikes targeted Ozon logistics facilities in Krasnodar, Dagestan, Stavropol, and Adygea.
Russia's defence ministry reported that three children were killed in Krasnodar following a drone attack.
Ozon shares dropped by as much as 12% on the Moscow Exchange following the overnight strikes.
The attacks follow recent Ukrainian strikes targeting warehouses belonging to Wildberries, Russia's largest online retailer.

title: US threat of ‘economic D-Day’ for Iran tests Trump’s China detente
author: John Power
content:
![oil](https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/oil-storage-1787537013.jpeg?resize=770%2C513&quality=80)
US President Donald Trump’s administration has said it aims to sever “every” economic lifeline sustaining Iran in what officials have warned will be the toughest sanctions campaign ever seen.
The threat, if followed through, would mean putting China, Iran’s biggest trade partner, squarely in the crosshairs of US sanctions.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items
- list 1 of 4Will Donald Trump’s new sanctions against Iran work?
- list 2 of 4Raphinha and Lopez score braces as Barcelona trounce Elche 5-0
- list 3 of 4Tokayev allies head for landslide victory in Kazakhstan elections
- list 4 of 4Large forest fire burns close to residential areas in Ankara
That would be a risky proposition for Washington due to the likelihood of severe blowback from Beijing – so much so that some analysts doubt that the Trump administration’s measures, set to be announced on Monday, will match its rhetoric in scope or severity.
While the Trump administration has yet to provide details about what it has dubbed “economic D-Day”, US officials have made it clear that Iran’s trade partners are in their sights.
In an op-ed in the Financial Times on Sunday, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned that countries fearful of breaking ties with Iran should not “discount the cost of testing Washington”.
“The president has created the conditions to leverage every agency, every authority and action many assumed we would never summon,” said Bessent, who is scheduled to unveil the sanctions in a news conference at 17:00 GMT.
![US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent speaks to reporters at the White House in Washington, DC, on August 20, 2026](https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/bessent-1787538201.jpeg?w=770&resize=770%2C522&quality=80)
Brett Erickson, a sanctions expert and managing principal of Obsidian Risk Advisors, said the Trump administration’s willingness to target China will be an indication of its resolve to mount a sustained economic offensive against Tehran.
“That is not a relationship you degrade lightly. If the United States decides to really bring China into the ring, it will be a serious indication that the United States plans to wage this economic war for a prolonged period of time,” Erickson told Al Jazeera.
“If they do not, it will be a tacit admission from the Trump administration that they do not believe economic hardship can seriously bring about a change in the Iranian position,” Erickson said.
Any US pressure campaign that excludes China would be necessarily limited in scope given the outsized importance of Beijing and Tehran’s economic ties.
China reported $9.96bn in two-way trade with Iran in 2025, a figure that does not include some $31.2bn in Iranian oil shipments, according to the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission.
China’s purchases of Iranian oil have been a particularly crucial lifeline for Tehran, accounting for about 90 percent of its oil sales, according to the US Treasury Department.
Until now, the Trump administration’s Iran sanctions regime has targeted only a handful of relatively minor China-based entities.
In April, the Trump administration sanctioned Hengli Petrochemical (Dalian) Refinery, one of China’s largest independent refineries, commonly known as “teapots”, over its alleged purchases of Iranian oil.
The Trump administration also imposed sanctions on four firms in Hong Kong in May, followed by measures in August targeting six China and Hong Kong-based shipping lines.
Washington has so far left Chinese financial institutions, widely viewed as a key node in Iran’s oil trade, untouched.
“Cutting off Chinese economic ties will be key to the success of any attempt to increase pressure on Iran. However, the United States won’t do it,” Jennifer Kavanagh, a senior fellow at Defense Priorities, a Washington-based foreign policy think tank, told Al Jazeera.
“If it does, China will retaliate and has the leverage to impose costs on the US,” Kavanagh said.
China has vigorously opposed US sanctions against Iran, arguing that economic pressure will not resolve the nearly six-month-long war.
In a statement on Sunday, China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said that Beijing remained “committed to promoting peace talks” and willing to “continue making efforts for the early restoration of peace and tranquility in the region”.
Iran, for its part, has threatened to retaliate against countries that support the US measures.
Mohsen Rezaei, the secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, warned on Saturday that any country that participated in sanctions would be considered an “enemy” and that “not a drop” of oil would leave the Gulf if Iran’s neighbours joined the US campaign.
Wang Wen, dean of the Chongyang Institute for Financial Studies at Renmin University of China, said Beijing would inevitably take countermeasures in response to any US sanctions and their intensity would depend on the “severity of US actions”.
“China maintains its desire to avoid conflict, but its bottom line cannot be crossed,” Wang told Al Jazeera.
For Trump, invoking Beijing’s ire would risk not only economic retaliation, but also unravelling efforts to stabilise US-China relations only weeks before the US president is due to host Chinese leader Xi Jinping at the White House.
Trump’s scheduled summit with Xi on September 24 would be their second face-to-face meeting aimed at lowering the temperature in US-China relations since Washington launched its war on Iran in late February, following Trump’s visit to Beijing in May.
![US President Donald Trump walks with China’s President Xi Jinping at the Zhongnanhai leadership compound, in Beijing, China, on May 15, 2026](https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/xi-1787552914.jpeg?w=770&resize=770%2C513&quality=80)
Zichen Wang, deputy secretary-general of the Center for China and Globalization (CCG) think tank in Beijing, said neither Beijing nor Washington were likely to want Iran to define the upcoming summit.
“Unless the US measures become very broad or directly target major Chinese interests, both sides are likely to try to keep this dispute from overwhelming the wider agenda,” Wang told Al Jazeera.
“That said, Chinese restraint should not be read as an absence of response,” Wang said.
“Beijing has often avoided immediate rhetorical escalation, but when unilateral US actions have materially affected Chinese companies or other Chinese interests, it has shown a growing willingness to answer with practical countermeasures.”
While the Trump administration could potentially make it more challenging and expensive for China to continue its economic support of Iran, it is unlikely to be able to stop Beijing outright if it is determined to maintain ties, said Erickson of Obsidian Risk Advisors.
“US sanctions can absolutely force companies to de-risk in order to avoid exposure, but there will always be an entity willing to fill this role,” Erickson said, adding that Xi is unlikely to “merely stand by while Trump flexes the powers of American economic statecraft without flexing Beijing’s own in return”.
Though US officials have stated their intention to “collapse” Iran’s government with ramped-up sanctions, Erickson expressed doubt that the Trump administration will be able to achieve its war goals through economic pressure alone.
“Unless the Trump administration is willing to burn serious bridges and employ all remaining levers of economic warfare simultaneously, there is no reasonable assertion that can be made that it will be able to produce the victory that kinetic warfare could not,” he said.
summary: The Trump administration has announced plans for severe new economic sanctions aimed at severing Iran's trade lifelines, a move that places China, Iran's largest trade partner, directly in the crosshairs. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned countries against testing Washington, setting up a test of the US-China detente just weeks before a planned summit between President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping. Analysts remain divided on whether the US will fully target major Chinese entities due to the risk of severe economic blowback and retaliation from Beijing.
key_points: The US administration plans to unveil its toughest-ever sanctions campaign against Iran, dubbed “economic D-Day.”
China is Iran's biggest trade partner and accounts for approximately 90 percent of Iranian oil sales.
Targeting Beijing risks economic retaliation and complicates efforts to stabilise US-China relations ahead of a summit between Trump and Xi Jinping.
China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated that Beijing opposes sanctions and will defend its interests with countermeasures if crossed.
Some analysts doubt the US will fully sever Chinese-Iranian economic ties because of Beijing's leverage and potential to impose costs on Washington.

title: Hawk fire: 90,000 told to evacuate as wildfire approaches Reno, Nevada
author: Ben Hatton
content:
Plumes of smoke seen over Reno as thousands evacuate due to wildfires
- Published
Tens of thousands of people have been told to evacuate from an area close to Reno, Nevada, as a large wildfire reached the outskirts of the city.
Around 42,000 people have been ordered to leave their homes immediately, with a further 45,000 people urged to get ready to leave.
The fire, which was first reported on Saturday morning, had so far injured six people, officials said. Windy and unpredictable weather conditions have contributed to its spread.
Nevada's Governor Joe Lombardo has declared a state of emergency in Washoe County and ordered the National Guard to join firefighting and law enforcement efforts.
"This is an active and rapidly evolving situation and I urge everyone in the affected areas to remain vigilant and follow the direction of local officials," he said.
The fire was caused by humans and first reported at 11:15 local time (18:15 GMT) on Saturday, according to local officials.
The Washoe emergency information centre said around 15,000 acres (23 sq miles) had been burned.
It said that, as of Sunday evening, no part of the fire's perimeter had yet been contained.
Around 13,700 homes were inside the evacuation area, local emergency services said, with two shelters set up to take in displaced residents.
Of the six injured, three were emergency responders fighting the fire.
![Two people look over what appears to be a domestic fence. They are looking at where smoke is rising from hills in the background.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/893/cpsprodpb/333b/live/32c86360-9f8b-11f1-9fae-bbc7231f436d.jpg)
![An image taken from a video shows a National Guard member in a helicopter - in the background outside are flames and smoke billowing](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/809/cpsprodpb/f4a7/live/33086ae0-9f91-11f1-b109-879e35c24276.jpg)
The Nevada National Guard said 72 personnel, one Chinook and one Black Hawk helicopter had joined the response
All Washoe County schools will be closed on Monday, except one, and mass road closures are in place.
The immediate "go now" evacuation zone and wider "get set" area - where people are being warned to prepare to evacuate - do not extend to the centre of Reno, but do affect large urban areas and part of a highway.
The University of Nevada in Reno - which has its main campus in the city, outside of but close to the "get set" warning area - said regular campus operations would continue but that it was monitoring the situation.
Large air tankers and helicopters have been flying over the area dropping water and fire retardants.
It's been named the Hawk Fire because it was first reported near the Hawk Meadow Trail, to the west of Reno.
Reno, in western Nevada, is located close to the state boundary with California and has a population of around 280,000 people.
